  vars <- intersect(vars, names(df))
  df %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(vars)) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(),
                     ~ sprintf("%d / %d (%.1f%%)",
                               sum(is.na(.)), length(.),
                               100 * mean(is.na(.))))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(),
                        names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(scope = label)
}

8.1 Cumulative terlipressin dose by day-0 route
Per-patient cumulative dose = sum of the daily total terlipressin dose, day 0 through day 13, missing daily dose treated as 0 (na.rm = TRUE). Cohorts: terli_route_day0 == 1 (Task 1, IV bolus) and == 2 (Task 2, continuous infusion).






Important



Column-name correction. The request listed total_dose_terli_day0 … total_dose_terli_day13, but the master dataset only has total_dose_terli_day0 under that name — the day 1–13 daily totals are stored as total_terli_day1 … total_terli_day13 (the word “dose” is dropped for days 1–13). This section uses the correct columns. Summing only total_dose_terli_day* (as literally written) would have collapsed the “cumulative” dose to just the day-0 value.




Show code
# Daily total terlipressin dose: day 0 uses total_dose_terli_day0;
# days 1-13 use total_terli_day{N} (naming differs in the export).
dose_vars_all <- c("total_dose_terli_day0", paste0("total_terli_day", 1:13))
dose_missing  <- setdiff(dose_vars_all, names(final_master))
dose_vars     <- intersect(dose_vars_all, names(final_master))
if (length(dose_missing) > 0) message("Dose columns not found: ", paste(dose_missing, collapse = ", "))

# route may be a factor by this point — coerce back to numeric safely
route_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(final_master$terli_route_day0)))

dose_df <- final_master %>%
  mutate(
    route_num = route_num,
    cumulative_dose = rowSums(
      across(all_of(dose_vars), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(.)))),
      na.rm = TRUE

  filter(route_num %in% c(1, 2)) %>%
  mutate(route = factor(route_num, levels = c(1, 2),
                        labels = c("IV bolus (route=1)", "Continuous infusion (route=2)")))

  group_by(route) %>%

8.2 Comparison of cumulative dose between routes (Task 3)
Normality screened per group (Shapiro–Wilk); both parametric (Welch t) and non-parametric (Mann–Whitney U) tests reported.

Both groups are right-skewed and non-normal → Mann–Whitney U is the primary test. The Welch t-test is unreliable here because two extreme values (day-0 = 701.7, day-2 = 425; see the data-quality flag above) inflate the bolus-group mean and hide the difference.
Duration confounding: cumulative dose reflects total exposure, not dosing intensity — a longer infusion accrues more drug at equal intensity. A dose-per-treatment-day comparison can be added later.

8.6 Model diagnostics (complete-case)
Effective sample, events, EPV, and a crude separation flag (any |β| > 10 or SE > 10, which signals quasi-complete separation — likely with few events + binary predictors). If flagged, treat ORs/CIs as unstable and consider Firth penalized logistic (logistf) as a later sensitivity analysis.


Show code
diag_row <- function(m, k, label) {
  b <- coef(summary(m))
  data.frame(
    Model                 = label,
    N                     = stats::nobs(m),
    Events                = sum(m$y),
    Covariates            = k,
    EPV                   = round(sum(m$y) / k, 1),
    `Separation?`         = ifelse(any(abs(b[, "Estimate"]) > 10 | b[, "Std. Error"] > 10,
                                        na.rm = TRUE), "YES — check", "no"),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}
